diagnostic_evidence.quote: Second, since \Cref{GD} is a subgradient method, in general it is not a descent method.

The result of the theorem then immediately follows from this observation, \Cref{Quasi Remark}, the facts that $t_k\rightarrow 0$, and $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} t_k=\infty$, and Theorem 1 in \cite{kiwiel2001convergence}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives the result solely from Kiwiel's subgradient framework (Theorem 1 in kiwiel2001convergence) under assumptions A1-A5 with t_k -> 0 and sum t_k = infinity, which yields only liminf-type convergence of the objective values. The appended clause asserts that the iterate values themselves decrease monotonically to kappa_*. Nothing in the argument enforces monotone decrease; quasisubgradient steps with a projection need not reduce kappa (the paper itself states the method 'in general it is not a descent method'), so kappa(cDo(d_k)) can increase along iterations and the claimed monotone convergence is unsupported and generally false. Only the running minimum, kappa_*^j = min_{k<=j} kappa(cDo(d_k)) (defined in the theorem but never used), is guaranteed to decrease to kappa_*.

failure_location.quote: It then holds that $\underline{\lim}_{k \rightarrow \infty} \kappa(\cDo(d_k))=\kappa_{*}$; in particular, $\kappa(\cDo(d_k))\downarrow \kappa_{*}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the final clause 'in particular, $\kappa(\cDo(d_k))\downarrow \kappa_{*}$' or replace it by the statement for the already-defined running minimum, i.e., $\kappa_{*}^{j}\downarrow\kappa_{*}$; the proof via Kiwiel's Theorem 1 then supports the statement as written.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence guarantee for Algorithm GD is reliable only in the liminf/best-so-far sense; the asserted monotone decrease kappa(cDo(d_k)) down to kappa_* is unsubstantiated. No other labelled result invokes this theorem, so no downstream loss.
issues.title: Asymptotic convergence theorem overclaims monotone decrease of the iterate values
issues.why_classification: A local deletion/rewording of one clause yields a correct theorem; the substantive asymptotic convergence guarantee (liminf of the values equals kappa_*) is fully preserved and no new argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the $\omega$-optimal diagonal scaling $D^{1/2}AD^{1/2}$ is given by $D = \alpha\Diag(\diag(A))^{-1}$, for any $\alpha > 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: In the paper's sense (identity is an omega-optimal diagonal scaling of A), the asserted 'only if' direction is false. The corollary's own first sentence gives the omega-optimal scaling D = alpha*Diag(diag(A))^{-1}; hence whenever diag(A) = alpha*e the identity scaling is omega-optimal, yet A need not be a multiple of the identity: for A = [[2,1],[1,2]], omega(DAD) = (d_1+d_2)/(sqrt(3)*sqrt(d_1 d_2)) >= 2/sqrt(3) with equality exactly at d proportional to e, so the identity is omega-optimal although A is not alpha*I. The gradient statement nabla_A omega(A) = 0 iff A = alpha*I concerns global minima of omega as a function on all of S^n_{++}; the stationarity condition relevant to diagonal preconditioning, derived in Theorem thm:optomegacomp (eq:statomega), is only diag(A) = (trace A/n)e. The cited mean-inequality equality conditions support the Jacobi-scaling sentence, not the stated biconditional, which is internally inconsistent with the corollary's first sentence.

failure_location.quote: The gradient $\nabla w(A)=0$ if, and only if, $A=\alpha I$ for some $\alpha >0$; i.e.,~$A$ is $\omega$-optimal if, and only if, it is a multiple of the identity.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second sentence by the correct characterization: A is omega-optimally diagonally preconditioned (the gradient of d -> omega(A Diag(d)) vanishes at d = e) if and only if diag(A) = alpha*e for some alpha > 0, which follows from eq:statomega together with pseudoconvexity; keep the first sentence unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The optimality characterization for omega-diagonal preconditioning in this corollary is wrong; a reader testing omega-optimality via A proportional to I would misclassify genuinely optimal scalings. The Jacobi-scaling sentence of the same corollary and all later uses (intro, Section 3.3, experiments) rely only on the valid part.
issues.title: False iff-characterization of omega-optimal diagonal scaling in cor:omegaoptDAD
issues.why_classification: The stated biconditional is false and must be replaced by a materially different (weaker) characterization, so this is more than a typo; but the replacement is a contained one-line restatement whose proof is already in the paper (eq:statomega), the corollary's main claim (Jacobi scaling optimal) survives, and no downstream labelled result depends on the false direction.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the paper's own convention A_i = R_i^TR_i with upper triangular R_i (used both in cor:added-2 and in Section sect:optblockdiag), the proposed blocks B_i = R_i^{-T} give BB^T = blkdiag(R_i^{-T}R_i^{-1}) = blkdiag((R_i R_i^T)^{-1}), whereas the omega-optimal scaling of Corollary cor:blckdiag satisfies Bbar*Bbar^T = blkdiag(A_i^{-1}) = blkdiag((R_i^TR_i)^{-1}). Since R_i R_i^T differs from R_i^T R_i in general, the two scalings have different spectra and different omega-values: for k = 1 and A = [[2,1],[1,1]] the choice B = R^{-T} yields spectrum {1/2, 2}, i.e., omega = 1.25, strictly worse than the omega-optimal value 1 attained by B_i = A_i^{-1/2}. The displayed eigenvalue identity concerns AD with D = blkdiag(R_i)blkdiag(R_i^T), a matrix different from the preconditioner product BB^T, so it does not support the claim; the claim only becomes correct with B_i = R_i^{-1} (equivalently, with the lower-Cholesky convention A_i = R_i R_i^T). The necessary identification of BB^T with blkdiag(A_i^{-1}) is thus not established and is false as stated.
